newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia retailers see good start to winter sales.
newsitem.headline: Australia retailers see good start to winter sales.

text.p: Australian department store retailers on Thursday said their cash tills were ringing up a good start to the winter sales season.
"Sales are up on expectations," said Jim Cooper, a spokesman at Coles Myer Ltd, Australia's largest retailer.
Coles Myer's major department store rival David Jones Ltd was also having a busy day.

"We are very pleased with the start," said Margaret McKenzie merchandising director at David Jones, an upmarket department store group. "We have had a very strong start to menswear, but most areas are performing very strongly," McKenzie said.
The retailers said there was now more consumer confidence than there had been earlier in the year.
On Wednesday, local economic data showed Australian retail sales rose 2.9 percent for the month of May, the highest since March 1994.
"The six weeks prior to the sales, we have seen a degree of improvement in the market place compared to earlier in the year," said David Jones' McKenzie.
"There appears to be a slight lift in consumer confidence which is encouraging."
The retailers also got a boost on Thursday from investors who were also seemed in a buying mood.
Retail shares ended Thursday higher than any other sector on the local bourse. Coles Myer closed 12.3 cents firmer at A$7.04, while David Jones finished three cents up at A$1.93.
